exposure: Prenatal exposure to air pollutants (PSI, SO2, CO, O3, PM2.5, PM10, NO, NO2, NOx)
cohort: The study included 253 Biliary Atresia patients and 2530 matched controls identified from 1,655,214 individuals born from first-time pregnancies in Taiwan between 2004 and 2016.
finding: No statistically significant association was found between prenatal air pollution exposure and the risk of Biliary Atresia in newborns, with no dose-response relationship observed.
